children.text: For the past two years, I’ve helped shape Spotify Technology, a new expression of Spotify built around the technology the company creates, not just the media it delivers.

Spotify has always been a technology company at its core. Spotify Technology turns that capability outward, creating a home for the products, platforms and tools originally built inside Spotify and now made available to other companies.
My role spanned brand, product design and design systems, helping establish a coherent vision for what business software from Spotify could look and feel like.

content.text: Building a new brand for Spotify

children.text: I helped shape the identity of Spotify Technology and the product brands that sit within it including Portal, Confidence, Backstage and Xirp.

The challenge was to create products with enough personality to stand on their own while making them unmistakably part of Spotify. This meant developing a shared visual language that could stretch across very different audiences, products and use cases without turning everything into the same brand.

content.text: A new design system for business tools

children.text: A key part of that work was exploring what business software at Spotify should look like. I helped shape the design-system strategy across these products, establishing shared foundations, components and patterns while bringing them closer to Spotify’s broader design language. The goal wasn’t simply consistency: it was to create a system that could give Spotify Technology its own point of view on how modern developer and business tools should feel.
Alongside the brand work, I worked across the products themselves to create a more consistent Spotify Technology product experience.

Rather than treating Portal, Confidence, Backstage and Serp as isolated tools, we started defining the patterns, interactions and principles that could connect them  creating the foundations for a family of products that increasingly feels like one ecosystem.

content.text: React Native App for Art Collectors

children.text: Docent is a radical new platform for art collectors to engage with contemporary art. Their mission is to bring a passionate expertise and a breadth of knowledge from across the contemporary art ecosystem together with the visionary research of leading scientists and thinkers in the realm of machine learning.

As a consultant, I was leading the product and design team as well as overseeing the product development. In the past 2 years working on this project I built the design system and all the new product experience. I also had the chance to code a significant part of the new structure we built on Expo.
We wanted to differentiate ourselves from existing competition by delivering a more immersive experience where you get the artwork in its biggest form. If you want to learn more, just swipe up.

children.text: We collaborated with the talented team at Numbered to produced Docent's landing page. The goal was to express the key concept of the app while still being true to our target audience.

Workplace is the all-in-one business communication platform from Meta. Think Facebook, but for your company. As part of a global improvement of the admin panel, I collaborated with researches, engineers and data scientist to create a new insights sections to help you understand your team better.
I worked directly with companies like Virgin, Heineken or RBS to test and improve our solutions. As a result, our new design was presented at the annual F8 conference.

I was part of the growth team at Workplace, leading the design for the new marketing site. The previous version was not in sync with the brand and modifications were very slow to come to life. To succeed, I had to align numerous different teams internally from brand, marketing, product and research. We also partnered with teams from conversion.com to help us validate some of our insights.

To target SMBs we imagined a visual structure that would mix both product elements and photography where people from our target could identify with. Some of these visuals were animated with videos in the background and moving UI elements.

content.text: Social Platform for early stage creators

children.text: Daisie is a social platform to help young creators connect with each other and build projects together. It is focused around ideas and storytelling with tools to share inspirations, prototypes and discuss creative projects.

I joined the team as the first designer, being responsible for the product design and research, from strategy to execution. We built the app and design system from the ground up for both mobile and web. This led to a launch with more than 22,000 sign ups on day one.

We used inspiration boards as a place for creators to share ideas and promote their work in a structured way, helping focusing on the content itself. We wanted to contrast with portfolios where you have complete freedom. Daisie was a place for inspiration and collaborative expression.
From strategy and design to development, I was responsible for the creation of marketing digital products for the restaurant, growth and consumer teams.
